prompt.String:
You are the plan navigator. Read the plan at `docs/iterations/068-member-name-editing/plan.md`, all relevant linked ADRs, designs and project guidance, the agreed domain scenarios and the current implementation. Coordinate implementation; do not implement product code, run application tests, refactor, review, publish or delegate to other agents yourself. The scenario child owns implementation and checks.

The planning commit leaves the plan's scenarios tagged `@todo`. Work only on the domain scenarios agreed in this plan. Leave browser journeys and other iterations' scenarios alone. Completing this workflow does not mean those other jobs or the whole iteration are released.

Choose the next scenario by what it adds to the implementation, not its position in a file. Prefer a small useful foundation that later scenarios can build on, then add constraints and complexity. Explain the choice using the plan, ADRs and existing code. Reconsider the next choice after every child finishes; do not prescribe the whole order in advance.

Keep ordinary notes in `.fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/progress.md`: scope, completed scenarios, current choice and why it is next. Record the exact iteration-plan path in `.fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/plan-path` for the child. On returning from a child, read its result and actual saved logs if needed, and inspect the updated feature tags and implementation. Keep completed work. A successful child removes its scenario's WIP tag; do not reactivate it.

For the next pending scenario, remove only its `@todo` tag and add `@wip`. There must be exactly one WIP domain scenario. Preserve every scenario's wording, assertions and other tags; don't remove any other scenario's todo tag. Save the previous `.fabro/tmp/bdd/` notes under `.fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/` before clearing that scratch directory for the next child, so it cannot mistake old evidence for its new assignment.

Choose `implement` only after preparing that single scenario. Choose `done` only when all agreed domain scenarios have completed, no in-scope todo remains and no WIP remains. Do not mark the iteration merged or claim review or publication.

End with `{"preferred_next_label":"implement"}` to call the scenario child, or `{"preferred_next_label":"done"}` to finish.

spec.graph_source:
digraph BddPlanImplementation {
    graph [goal="Implement the planned domain scenarios, one at a time; do not publish",
        default_max_retries=0,
        model_stylesheet="* { provider: openai; model: gpt-5.6-sol; reasoning_effort: high; }"]
    start [shape=Mdiamond]
    done [shape=Msquare]
    stop [shape=parallelogram, script="echo 'Plan implementation stopped; work is preserved.' >&2; exit 1"]
    setup [shape=parallelogram, script="mkdir -p .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan && git rev-parse HEAD > .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/base"]
    navigator [shape=box, backend="api", fidelity="full", thread_id="bdd-plan-navigator", prompt="@../../../prompts/navigator.md"]
    scenario [shape=house, stack.child_workflow="../../double.fabro"]

    start -> setup
    setup -> navigator [condition="outcome=succeeded"]
    setup -> stop
    navigator -> scenario [condition="outcome=succeeded && preferred_label=implement"]
    navigator -> observe [condition="outcome=succeeded && preferred_label=done"]
    navigator -> stop
    scenario -> navigator [condition="outcome=succeeded"]
    scenario -> stop
    observe [shape=parallelogram, script="set -eu; mkdir -p .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/eval; cp acceptance-tests/features/member_profile.feature .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/eval/final.feature; git diff \"$(cat .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/base)\" -- web/lib > .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/eval/code.patch; git diff --name-only \"$(cat .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/base)\" > .fabro/tmp/bdd-plan/eval/changed-paths"]
    observe -> done [condition="outcome=succeeded"]
    observe -> stop
}

agent_tools.name: apply_patch
agent_tools.description: Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

agent_tools.name: close_agent
agent_tools.description: Close a running or completed subagent that is no longer needed.

agent_tools.name: request_user_input
agent_tools.description: Ask the human one or more questions and wait for their answers before continuing this stage.

agent_tools.name: send_input
agent_tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running agent receives it at a safe turn boundary. A completed agent starts another turn in the same session with its existing history.

agent_tools.name: shell_command
agent_tools.description:
Runs a shell command and returns its output.
- Always set the `workdir` param rather than using `cd`.
- Reading and searching files goes through this tool: prefer `rg` and `rg --files`, which are much faster than alternatives like `grep` and `find`.
- Use `apply_patch` to edit files, not `cat`, heredocs, or other shell write tricks.
- `timeout_ms` defaults to 10000 ms and is capped at 600000 ms. A command that timed out once will time out again, so raise the timeout rather than retrying.

agent_tools.name: spawn_agent
agent_tools.description: Spawn a subagent for independent work or context isolation. Use it for tasks that can proceed separately, and avoid duplicating the same work in the parent session.

agent_tools.name: update_plan
agent_tools.description: Update the multi-step plan for the current task. Submit the entire plan; existing steps are reconciled by exact step text.

agent_tools.name: wait
agent_tools.description: Wait for a subagent to complete, then use the result to synthesize the outcome for the user.
